# Analyze the relationship between introduction pathways and minimum residence time (mrt) in the invasion_success dataset
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Check the distribution of mrt across different introduction pathways
sns.boxplot(x='intro.pathway', y='mrt', data=invasion_success)
plt.title('Distribution of Minimum Residence Time (mrt) by Introduction Pathway')
plt.xlabel('Introduction Pathway')
plt.ylabel('Minimum Residence Time (mrt)')
plt.show()

# Check for statistical significance using ANOVA
from scipy.stats import f_oneway

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt' and 'intro.pathway'
filtered_data = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'intro.pathway'])

# Group the data by 'intro.pathway' and extract the 'mrt' values
groups = filtered_data.groupby('intro.pathway')['mrt'].apply(list)

# Perform ANOVA
f_statistic, p_value = f_oneway(*groups)
f_statistic, p_value

# Analyze the relationship between introduction pathways, mrt, and invasion success metrics
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

# Fit a linear model to examine the interaction between 'intro.pathway' and 'mrt' on 'number.of.invaded.plots'
model = ols('number.of.invaded.plots ~ C(intro.pathway) * mrt', data=invasion_success).fit()
anova_table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
anova_table

# Fit a linear model to examine the interaction between 'intro.pathway' and 'mrt' on 'area.of.occupancy.10km'
model_area = ols('area.of.occupancy.10km ~ C(intro.pathway) * mrt', data=invasion_success).fit()
anova_table_area = sm.stats.anova_lm(model_area, typ=2)
anova_table_area

from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

# Group the data by 'intro.pathway' and calculate the mean 'number.of.invaded.plots' and 'area.of.occupancy.10km' for each group
groups = invasion_success.groupby('intro.pathway')

# Perform pairwise t-tests for 'number.of.invaded.plots' across pathways
for pathway1, pathway2 in combinations(groups.groups.keys(), 2):
    group1 = groups.get_group(pathway1)['number.of.invaded.plots']
    group2 = groups.get_group(pathway2)['number.of.invaded.plots']
    t_stat, p_val = ttest_ind(group1, group2)
    print(f"t-test between {pathway1} and {pathway2} for 'number.of.invaded.plots': t={t_stat:.2f}, p={p_val:.4f}")

# Perform pairwise t-tests for 'area.of.occupancy.10km' across pathways
for pathway1, pathway2 in combinations(groups.groups.keys(), 2):
    group1 = groups.get_group(pathway1)['area.of.occupancy.10km']
    group2 = groups.get_group(pathway2)['area.of.occupancy.10km']
    t_stat, p_val = ttest_ind(group1, group2)
    print(f"t-test between {pathway1} and {pathway2} for 'area.of.occupancy.10km': t={t_stat:.2f}, p={p_val:.4f}")
